text: A task leaves your list in one of two ways: the work got done, or it no longer needs doing. Scout records which, so the history tells the truth.
The one thing to remember: Mark done means the work is done. The x, Remove, means it no longer needs doing, and you say why.
The car's ear cleaner was restocked this morning.
So click Mark done.
This one is a duplicate. Nobody needs to do it.
Click the x.
A reason is required. Pick one, or type your own.
Duplicate of another task.
Remove task.
This one is shared with Dr. Lane. Each of you has your own copy.
The recheck is booked, so click Mark done.
Scout asks whether to close Dr. Lane's copy too, or just yours.
The work is finished for both of you, so Close for everyone.
Click Completed.
Each one is labeled Done or Removed, so anyone can see what really happened.
Marked something done by mistake? Open it.
Click Reopen.
It goes back on the list for the same person.
Reopen.

The most common mistakes: marking a task done when you've only started it, and removing a task just because you can't get to it. Use Move to hand it on instead. Remember: Mark done means the work is done; Remove means it no longer needs doing.
